newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Further slipping in cash beef prices and expectations of further weakness ahead in cash cattle as seasonal fed cattle supplies rise were expected to encourage early pressure in live cattle futures, analysts said.
However, the discount of futures to cash and expectations boxed beef values may firm by midweek as warmer temperatures increase outdoor grilling could support prices, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to show early support following another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index and indications for lower corn futures. Cash feeder markets continue to trend higher, analysts said.

Although demand for replacement feeders may decline as fed cattle prices ease, improved pasture conditions and recent death losses in the northern plains remain supporting factors in cash feeders, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.24 at $72.78 per cwt, the highest price level since February 17, 1995.
